title: About PACE GK Academy and Why Choose PACE
heading: What is PACE?
text:
[About PACE GK Academy and Why Choose PACE > What is PACE?]
PACE stands for **Pakistan Academy of Competitive Exams** (website brand: PACE GK Academy). It is an online test-preparation platform for Pakistani competitive and public-service exams, mainly PPSC (Punjab Public Service Commission) and FPSC (Federal Public Service Commission), and also ITS, ECP, MOD, ASF, Islamabad Police, FIA, FGEI and ANF tests.

Page title: "PACE GK Academy: Pakistan Academy For Competitive Exams". Site description: PACE provides preparation in Reading, Quiz and PPSC Mock Test formats from PPSC past papers, and at the end generates a result according to PPSC.

title: About PACE GK Academy and Why Choose PACE
heading: Mission (About page)
text:
[About PACE GK Academy and Why Choose PACE > Mission (About page)]
PACE is described as a best solution for online test preparation, specially designed for students who want to prepare for one-paper tests in the shortest possible time.

PACE provides test preparation in **three formats**:
1. Reading mode
2. Quiz mode
3. PPSC Mock Test

At the end of a quiz it generates a **result card**, and users can also check wrongly attempted questions. Questions can be searched **paper-wise, department-wise, subject-wise and year-wise**.

text:
[PACE GK Academy — Frequently Asked Questions]
Source: https://www.pacegkacademy.com/FAQ (Pakistan Academy of Competitive Exams)

**Q: How are online classes conducted?**
A: It is very easy. You are added into a class WhatsApp group and a Zoom App link is shared with you for the respective lecture.

**Q: What is the mechanism of the Testing (Test) Series?**
A: An MCQ-based paper is shared with students on a Google Form. They solve the paper and the application shows results on submission. The test is also discussed with them afterwards.

**Q: Queries about registration?**
A: You have to pay the fee on the given account details and share screenshots of that payment on the PACE WhatsApp numbers (+92 300 1757495, +92-345-0668111).

**Q: What is the required qualification for Public Service Exams?**
A: A Second Division or Grade C degree holder recognised by the Higher Education Commission can apply for these exams. Candidates with a Third Division or Grade D are also eligible for various jobs.

title: PACE GK Academy — Frequently Asked Questions
text:
[PACE GK Academy — Frequently Asked Questions]
**Q: What is the required age limit for jobs through the commission?**
A: It includes an age range of 21–35 years. However, it may vary from job to job requirement.

**Q: What is the syllabus for general one-paper exams?**
A: An MCQ-based written paper covering 8–10 compulsory subjects such as General Knowledge, Current Affairs, Math, English, Islamiat, Computer, Pak Study and General Science.

**Q: What is prohibited in the examination hall?**
A: Calculators, mobiles, digital watches, arms, ammunition and books are not allowed during exams. No one is allowed to write on the question paper and take it home.

**Q: What possible jobs are announced by commissions?**
A: The range of job announcements is very vast and may differ from commission to commission.

heading: PPSC Mock Test (https://www.pacegkacademy.com/PPSC-Paper-Instructions)
text:
[Mock Test, Quiz Mode, Reading Mode and Make Paper > PPSC Mock Test (https://www.pacegkacademy.com/PPSC-Paper-Instructions)]
A simulated PPSC-style paper that generates a result like PPSC. Students describe it as the site's unique feature.
**Paper instructions shown before the test starts:**
1. Read the instructions carefully before you start answering.
2. Only **90 minutes for 100 questions** is allowed.
3. Read the question paper carefully and check your answer.
4. Each question has four options. Click only one check button for the answer you think is correct.
5. Each question carries **1 mark** and **0.25 mark is deducted for each incorrect answer** (negative marking).
6. Use of a calculator is not allowed.
7. If a candidate has any observation on the paper, they may bring it to notice in the "Leave A Reply" section.
The user must tick a box confirming they have read the instructions.

text:
[Articles & Insights — English Tests (IELTS, TOEFL, PTE) and GRE > 2. How to Score 320+ in GRE — Tips & Resources]
URL: https://www.pacegkacademy.com/How-to-score-320-plus-in-GRE-tips-and-resources
- A 320 means roughly 160 Verbal + 160 Quant. Study time: 8–12 weeks (intensive); plan adjustable to 8–16 weeks.
- **Strategy:** take a full-length diagnostic (official ETS GRE practice); focus on Quant fundamentals and Verbal vocabulary; timed sections; answer elimination and pacing; review mistakes; use spaced repetition (Anki/Magoosh Vocab); simulate test day with at least 4 full-length tests.
- **12-week plan:** Weeks 1–2 diagnostic, math fundamentals, 20–30 new vocab words/day. Weeks 3–6 timed Quant & Verbal practice 3×/week, learn problem types (DS, PS, RC, SC), one full-length test at week 6. Weeks 7–12 polish weak areas, one simulated test per week, time management, last 2 weeks taper and rest.
- **Resources:** Official GRE/ETS POWERPREP, Magoosh GRE, Manhattan Prep, Kaplan GRE, Princeton Review, Anki.
- **Test-day tips:** book a slot when you are sharpest; arrive early; mark and skip hard questions; use the on-screen calculator where allowed; stay hydrated; avoid heavy study the night before.

heading: 4. PTE vs IELTS — Which Test Should You Take?
text:
[Articles & Insights — English Tests (IELTS, TOEFL, PTE) and GRE > 4. PTE vs IELTS — Which Test Should You Take?]
URL: https://www.pacegkacademy.com/PTE-vs-IELTS-Which-Test-Should-You-Take

| Feature | PTE Academic | IELTS (Academic & General) |
|---|---|---|
| Format | Fully computer-based; speaking via microphone | Paper or computer; speaking with a human examiner |
| Duration | ~2 hours | ~2 h 45 min (varies) |
| Scoring | 10–90 | Band 0–9 |
| Results | Usually within 48 hours | Paper ~13 days; computer ~3–5 days |
| Acceptance | Many universities and some governments; growing | Most universities, governments, professional bodies |
| Cost | Varies by country | Varies by country |

**Rough score mapping:** PTE 79–90 ≈ IELTS 8.5–9.0; 65–78 ≈ 7.0–8.0; 59–64 ≈ 6.5; 50–58 ≈ 5.5–6.0; 30–49 ≈ 4.0–5.0.
**PTE suits:** fast typists comfortable with microphones, want quick results. **IELTS suits:** prefer a human speaking examiner or need widest acceptance.
